newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta closes lower as Chidambaram dashes hopes.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta closes lower as Chidambaram dashes hopes.

text.p: Share prices weakened further and closed lower at the Calcutta bourse as foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and Indian mutual funds stepped up selling pressure, brokers said.
They said that a mid-session recovery was aborted following a fresh selling spree towards the close of trade and most blue-chips lost ground rapidly.
Brokers said that even shares of mid-cap companies which moved up marginally last week dipped as retail investors were selling out to exit from an uncertain secondary market.

"There are signs of virtual panic selling. Even leading foreign funds are selling off holdings of their favourite scrips. The technicals too do not look very good," said Aprajit Sharma of brokers Jet Age Securities.

"Volumes too were very low. Today was also the last day of accounting period at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and this depressed prices at the local bourse too as there were no orders from traders in Bombay."
Another analyst said: "The Indian finance minister announced sops for the capital markets but this did not contain anything for retail investors."

"FIIs have been allowed to invest 100 percent of their funds in debt but expected incentives like exemption of dividend income from tax did not materialise. This has created disappointment among investors," he added.
